wp2shell WordPress RCE Exploitation and Hugging Face AI-Agent Breach Lead Threat Digest

wp2shell and SonicWall SMA1000 zero-days join Hugging Face AI-agent breach
item.content:encoded:
Critical ServiceNow code execution flaw now exploited in attacks — Must Read

Attackers are now exploiting CVE-2026-6875, a critical pre-authentication remote code execution flaw in ServiceNow AI Platform, just days after patches were released. ServiceNow customers with self-hosted instances should upgrade to a fixed version immediately.

  • Attackers have begun exploiting CVE-2026-6875, a critical vulnerability in the ServiceNow AI Platform, according to threat intelligence company Defused.
  • Searchlight Cyber found and reported the flaw on April 1st, saying it allows unauthenticated threat actors to escape the sandbox and execute code remotely within the ServiceNow platform in high-complexity attacks.
  • ServiceNow addressed the flaw across hosted instances and released security updates for self-hosted instances on July 13th.
  • Defused said the observed payloads target the same pre-authentication sink at /assessment_thanks.do documented by Searchlight Cyber, but use a different sandbox-escape route than the published proof of concept.
  • ServiceNow’s official advisory still says the company is not currently aware of exploitation against ServiceNow instances, while advising customers to upgrade to a patched release as soon as possible.

SonicWall SMA1000 flaws exploited as zero-days to push custom malware — Must Read

SonicWall SMA1000 vulnerabilities CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410 were exploited as zero-days for weeks to gain root access and deploy custom malware on VPN appliances. Customers should urgently apply SonicWall’s patches to versions 12.4.3-03453 or 12.5.0-02835.

  • Two recently disclosed SonicWall SMA1000 vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410, were exploited as zero-days for weeks to install custom malware on vulnerable VPN appliances.
  • The flaws affect SonicWall SMA1000 6210, 7210, and 8200v appliances, and SonicWall released patches in versions 12.4.3-03453 and 12.5.0-02835.
  • Volexity found that threat actor UTA0533 abused the SMA1000 /wsproxy endpoint to create unauthenticated WebSocket tunnels to internal services, including CouchDB and the appliance management service.
  • After obtaining the appliance product_uuid, the attackers exploited the sysCtrl.execRemoveHotfix RPC method to execute commands as root and take full control of the appliance.
  • UTA0533 installed KNUCKLEBALL to deploy the Java-based malware families Sou5 and ORANGETAIL, and also modified nginx configuration to expose the ORANGETAIL webshell remotely.

A Look Inside the HuggingFace Breach — Must Read

HuggingFace disclosed a breach where an autonomous AI attacker exploited RCE flaws in its dataset processing pipeline to steal credentials and move laterally, while defenders used AI-driven detection to investigate and contain it. The key takeaway is that AI/ML workloads and downloaded datasets must be treated as untrusted code with strict least privilege and monitoring for unusual access patterns.

  • On July 16, 2026, HuggingFace disclosed a security breach in which an autonomous AI attacker infiltrated its internal infrastructure.
  • The attacker exploited two remote code execution vulnerabilities in HuggingFace’s dataset processing pipeline, including abuse of a remote-code dataset loader and template injection in a dataset configuration.
  • The attacker leaked cloud and cluster credentials, moved laterally into several internal clusters, and generated decoy activity to complicate attribution and impact analysis.
  • HuggingFace detected the compromise with an AI-assisted threat detection system and used LLM-driven analysis agents to extract indicators of compromise from logs.
  • HuggingFace recommended that users rotate API access tokens and report any unusual account activity.

Russian Intelligence Hacks IP Cameras to Spy on Military Logistics Across NATO States and Ukraine — Must Read

Dutch intelligence says Russian state actors are hijacking exposed IP cameras across Ukraine and NATO/EU countries to monitor military logistics, weapons shipments, and troop movements. The main fix is basic but urgent: remove cameras from the public internet, change default credentials, patch them, and control what they can see.

  • The AIVD and MIVD said at least one Russian intelligence service is systematically hijacking internet-connected security cameras across Europe and Ukraine to monitor military transport routes, weapons shipments bound for Kyiv, and Ukrainian troop locations.
  • In Ukraine, access to compromised cameras has been used in attempts to neutralise Ukrainian military personnel and destroy their equipment, according to the Dutch intelligence services.
  • The operators reportedly find exposed devices by scanning the internet, identifying camera brands, and accessing cameras that still use default passwords, obsolete firmware, or unchanged factory settings.
  • Censys counted more than 87,000 internet-connected cameras across the EU, NATO members, and Ukraine running a service version matching a known-exploited vulnerability, including more than 4,000 in Ukraine.
  • The Dutch services said they had confirmed only a small number of breached cameras in the Netherlands, located directly on military logistics routes, and had warned the organisations operating them.

Estée Lauder discloses data breach via Oracle E-Business flaw — Must Read

Estée Lauder is notifying affected individuals after attackers exploited an Oracle E-Business Suite HR system flaw to steal sensitive personal, financial, health, and employment data. The incident appears tied to the Clop mass-exploitation campaign using CVE-2025-61882.

  • Estée Lauder is notifying customers of a data breach after hackers exploited a flaw in Oracle E-Business Suite used by the company for human resources operations.
  • The company determined on June 19, 2026, that an unauthorized third party had accessed the Oracle E-Business Suite system on or around August 9, 2025, and obtained personal information of certain individuals.
  • The exposed data includes full names, postal addresses, email addresses, dates of birth, Social Security numbers, passport numbers, financial account information, health information, and employment information such as payroll and performance reports.
  • The breach date correlates with a mass-exploitation campaign targeting Oracle E-Business Suite through CVE-2025-61882, which Google and Mandiant linked to the Clop ransomware gang in October 2025.
  • Estée Lauder is advising recipients to watch for signs of identity theft and fraud and is offering 24 months of complimentary identity monitoring services through Kroll.

JadePuffer agentic attacks now target AI model data with ransomware — Must Read

JadePuffer has upgraded its autonomous ransomware operations with EncForge, malware built to encrypt AI and machine learning assets such as model checkpoints, training datasets, and vector databases. Sysdig says the attacker exploited a vulnerable Langflow instance and exposed Docker socket, highlighting the need to patch Langflow and lock down container access.

  • Sysdig reported that the JadePuffer autonomous AI agent returned to a previously breached Langflow instance vulnerable to CVE-2025-3248 and deployed the Go-based EncForge ransomware.
  • EncForge targets about 180 file extensions across AI and machine learning environments, including model checkpoints, vector databases, training datasets, embedding indices, Hugging Face SafeTensors files, PyTorch and TensorFlow models, GGUF and GGML weights, and FAISS vector indexes.
  • After discovering an exposed Docker socket with root-level control, the attacker developed and deployed six Python scripts in five minutes to solve ransomware delivery problems.
  • EncForge uses AES-256 in counter mode with an RSA-2048 public key to encrypt selected portions of files, appends the .locked extension, and drops a ransom note with a unique identifier.
  • Sysdig found no evidence of data exfiltration during the intrusion and recommended updating to Langflow 1.3.0 or later, restricting Docker socket access, running Langflow containers as non-root, and applying filesystem-level access controls to model weight directories.

Exposed Server Reveals AI-Assisted Phishing Toolkit Behind WebDAV Malware Campaign — Must Read

Rapid7 found an exposed malware delivery server containing an AI-assisted phishing toolkit, including WebDAV-based Windows delivery experiments and live campaigns targeting Mexican users via a fake government ID lookup site. The key takeaway is that attackers are using commodity AI coding tools to rapidly build, test, and scale phishing delivery pipelines around patched and emerging Windows abuse techniques.

  • Rapid7 found an exposed malware delivery server containing 1,048 files, including lure templates, filename-spoofing tests, execution experiments, droppers, builder notes, and two campaign chains.
  • The most developed test set focused on CVE-2025-33053, a WebDAV working-directory hijack that abuses a .url shortcut to launch a signed Windows binary while pointing its working directory at an attacker-controlled WebDAV share.
  • Rapid7 assessed that the READMEs, lure-generation guides, test write-ups, mapping files, and emoji-heavy phishing-site JavaScript reflected an LLM-assisted workflow likely built with help from the open-source Coderrr AI coding tool.
  • An active campaign targeting Mexican users used the typosquat gobf.mx to imitate a government CURP national-ID lookup site and delivered a .scr executable disguised as a PDF report.
  • The delivery panel logged 77,098 requests from 3,892 unique IPs across 101 countries over roughly 5.5 days, with Mexico accounting for 82.5% of traffic and 96.9% of launch activity.

FakeGit Campaign Uses 7,600 GitHub Repositories to Spread SmartLoader Malware — Should Read

Researchers found a large FakeGit campaign using about 7,600 malicious GitHub repositories, including hundreds disguised as AI skills and MCP servers, to spread SmartLoader and ultimately StealC malware. The key risk is “AgentBaiting,” where AI agents like ChatGPT, Claude Code, or Gemini can discover and recommend these fake repositories without a user being sent a malicious link.

  • Researchers found nearly 7,600 malicious GitHub repositories in the FakeGit campaign, with more than 800 posing as AI skills or Model Context Protocol servers to deliver SmartLoader malware.
  • FakeGit uses copied projects, lookalike developer profiles, convincing README files, and malicious ZIP files to deliver SmartLoader, which can establish persistence and push secondary payloads such as the StealC information stealer.
  • Island said FakeGit has an AI-powered evolution called AgentBaiting, where an AI agent searching for a skill or MCP server can discover a bogus GitHub repository and pass the attacker’s instructions to a user.
  • Island’s tests found Anthropic Claude Code, Google Gemini, and OpenAI ChatGPT susceptible to surfacing malicious campaign repositories without being shown a link.
  • As of July 2026, the FakeGit operation had recorded more than 14 million downloads across GitHub Release assets in about 200 campaign repositories.

Targeted Attack on Government Entities in the Middle East | Part 1 — Should Read

Zscaler ThreatLabz analyzed a July 2026 campaign targeting Middle Eastern government entities in which an East Asia-linked actor used a multi-stage malware chain involving TELESHIM, MIXEDKEY, and BINDCLOAK. The attackers abused Telegram for command-and-control, used heavy obfuscation and anti-analysis techniques, and encrypted the final payload with a key tied to each victim machine.

  • In July 2026, Zscaler ThreatLabz observed activity by a threat actor linked to East Asia targeting government entities in the Middle East.
  • The campaign used a multi-stage attack chain that began with an ISO file containing a legitimate ASUSTek RegSchdTask.exe file that sideloaded a malicious AsTaskSched.dll DLL.
  • ThreatLabz identified previously undocumented malware tooling in the campaign, including TELESHIM, MIXEDKEY, and BINDCLOAK.
  • TELESHIM abused the Telegram API for command-and-control communication and used anti-analysis techniques including heavy disk I/O activity, CPUID hypervisor detection, and a WMI RAM speed check.
  • MIXEDKEY decrypted and reflectively loaded the final BINDCLOAK payload using a key derived from the infected machine’s volume serial number.

HollowGraph Malware Hides C2 and Stolen Files in Microsoft 365 Events Dated 2050 — Should Read

HollowGraph is a newly reported espionage implant that hides command-and-control instructions and stolen files inside Microsoft 365 calendar events dated in 2050, using legitimate Microsoft Graph API traffic to blend in. Defenders should hunt for far-future calendar events with suspicious subjects or attachments, audit Graph app permissions and client secrets, and check for indicators such as cloudlanecdn[.]com and logAzure.txt.

  • Group-IB identified HollowGraph, a .NET DLL espionage implant that uses a hijacked Microsoft 365 calendar as a two-way command and data channel through legitimate Microsoft Graph API traffic.
  • HollowGraph reads operator instructions from an attachment on a calendar event dated 2050-05-13 and exfiltrates encrypted stolen files by creating far-future events with attachments.
  • The implant supports only two commands, get and send, and encrypts calendar-carried data with hybrid RSA and AES-256 encryption using separate key pairs for incoming and outgoing data.
  • HollowGraph refreshes its Entra ID login details over DNS by decoding tenant ID, client ID, client secret, and target mailbox values from IPv6 AAAA records returned by cloudlanecdn[.]com, then writes them to logAzure.txt.
  • Group-IB found HollowGraph on at least 12 machines, observed victim traffic from 3 June to 9 July 2026, and tied the malware with high confidence to Cavern while declining to attribute the campaign to a specific threat actor.

Russian-Speaking Hacker Uses Google Gemini CLI to Control Botnet of Eight Dental Clinic PCs — Should Read

A Russian-speaking threat actor known as “bandcampro” used Google Gemini CLI as a hands-on hacking assistant to migrate and operate a small botnet controlling eight dental clinic PCs. The case shows how AI agents can make command-and-control infrastructure cheap, portable, and quickly rebuildable, reducing the impact of takedowns and lowering the skill needed for cybercrime.

  • Trend Micro analyzed 200 Gemini CLI session logs from March 19 to April 21, 2026, showing a Russian-speaking threat actor known as “bandcampro” using Google Gemini CLI for hacking-related tasks.
  • The actor used Gemini CLI to deploy and operate command-and-control infrastructure for a small botnet controlling eight computers at a dental clinic and accessing its OpenDental database.
  • Gemini CLI helped migrate the command-and-control setup to a new virtual private server, configure Cloudflare tunnels, manage bots, and debug connectivity issues within minutes.
  • The article says the entire command-and-control operation fit into three plaintext files totaling about 5 KB, making the infrastructure easy to replicate and rebuild on a fresh server.
  • The actor also used the AI agent for password cracking, WordPress admin panel brute forcing, analysis of 1Password dumps, and planning a phone-based cryptocurrency fraud scheme targeting elderly people in the U.S. and Canada.

Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity hit by sandbox escapes — Should Read

Researchers found sandbox escape flaws in Cursor, OpenAI Codex, Google Gemini CLI, and Antigravity where AI coding agents could write workspace files that trusted tools outside the sandbox later executed or loaded. Most issues have been patched, but the findings show a broader risk in agentic coding tools that trust project files as safe input.

  • Pillar Security researchers broke out of the sandboxes in Cursor, OpenAI's Codex, Google's Gemini CLI, and Antigravity by having the agent write files that trusted tools outside the sandbox later ran, loaded, or scanned.
  • The researchers said prompt injection can trigger the issue when a malicious instruction is planted in a README, an issue, a dependency, or a diff and becomes a local action on the developer's machine.
  • Pillar Security grouped the seven findings into four failure modes: denylist sandboxes, executable workspace configuration, command allowlists that trust command names rather than arguments, and privileged local daemons outside the sandbox.
  • Most of the issues are patched and vendor-acknowledged, including Cursor fixes in version 3.0.0 and an OpenAI Codex CLI fix in version 0.95.0.
  • Google classified the two Antigravity findings as “Other valid security vulnerabilities” and downgraded them because it judged them difficult to exploit due to social engineering or repository-trust requirements.

Romania races to restore land registry after cyberattack disrupts property market — Should Read

Romania’s land registry systems remain offline after a cyberattack disrupted the country’s fully digital property transaction process, though officials say core cadastral and legal databases were not compromised. Authorities are migrating systems to the government cloud and investigating a financially motivated threat actor who exploited known vulnerabilities and leaked credentials.

  • Romania's National Agency for Cadastre and Land Registration said a cyberattack disabled its central IT infrastructure, including the nationwide e-Terra cadastral and land registry platform.
  • The outage disrupted online land registry services, official email systems, and applications used by notaries, lawyers, cadastral specialists, and ANCPI employees, preventing new property registrations and processing of existing requests.
  • ANCPI said its technical and legal databases containing cadastral information, ownership details, and mortgages had not been compromised.
  • Authorities have begun migrating applications to the Romanian government cloud and said services will be gradually restored after system integrity is verified.
  • Romania's cyber security director Dan Cimpean said the attack appeared financially motivated and used known software vulnerabilities and previously leaked credentials.

SleeperGem Uses Three Malicious RubyGems Packages to Target Developer Machines — Should Read

Researchers found three malicious RubyGems packages used in a supply-chain attack called SleeperGem that targeted developer machines, avoided CI environments, and installed a persistent native backdoor. Users who installed the affected gems should treat their systems and credentials as compromised and rotate secrets.

  • Cybersecurity researchers identified a software supply chain attack called SleeperGem involving three malicious RubyGems packages: git_credential_manager, Dendreo, and fastlane-plugin-run_tests_firebase_testlab.
  • StepSecurity said each malicious release acts as a loader that fetches a second stage from an attacker-controlled Forgejo host, skips build systems, and installs a native daemon with persistence on developer machines.
  • The git_credential_manager package impersonates Microsoft Git Credential Manager, while Dendreo and fastlane-plugin-run_tests_firebase_testlab had been dormant for years before receiving malicious updates.
  • The malware checks for about 30 environment variables associated with CI services such as GitHub Actions, GitLab, CircleCI, Travis, Jenkins, and Vercel, and exits if any are found.
  • Users who installed any of the affected gems are advised to treat their machines and associated secrets as compromised, remove the dropped daemon and persistence methods, check for a setuid shell at /usr/local/sbin/ping6, and rotate all credentials.

Hackers steal $23.7 million in crypto from Ostium in off-chain attack — Should Read

Ostium says hackers stole $23.75 million from its liquidity provider vault by compromising off-chain price-feed infrastructure and submitting fake price reports to generate artificial trading profits. Trader collateral and existing positions were not stolen, but trading remains paused while Ostium secures systems and investigates.

  • Ostium said an attacker stole $23.75 million from its liquidity provider vault after compromising off-chain infrastructure used to feed prices into the protocol.
  • The attacker submitted illegitimate price reports disguised as valid ones and rapidly opened and closed large positions to generate artificial profits.
  • Ostium said trader collateral was held in a separate contract, was not stolen, and existing long and short positions were not closed or liquidated.
  • According to PeckShieldAlert, the exploiter swapped the stolen USDC for 12,080 Ethereum and deposited 10,540 Ethereum to TornadoCash.
  • Trading on Ostium was paused within 60 minutes of the first exploit transaction and remained paused five days after the incident.

India says allegedly leaked nuclear plant files pose no safety risk — Should Read

India’s nuclear operator said files allegedly leaked from a Kudankulam contractor breach relate only to non-nuclear support infrastructure and do not affect plant safety or security. The data was claimed by World Leaks after a Reliance Infrastructure-hosted server incident.

  • India's Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited said the allegedly leaked Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant documents relate only to conventional Balance of Plant common service facilities and not to nuclear safety or security systems.
  • World Leaks published files that appeared to include engineering drawings, supplier information, inspection records, and insurance documents related to Kudankulam Units 3 and 4, which are under construction.
  • Reliance Group said it suffered a partial breach involving data stored on infrastructure hosted by Indian data center provider Yotta, while Yotta said it stopped suspicious activity on a Reliance Infrastructure server in late May.
  • Independent researcher Rakesh Krishnan said nearly 19,000 files totaling about 14.3 GB related to Kudankulam were published by World Leaks, though the authenticity of the documents could not be independently verified.
  • Kudankulam previously experienced a 2019 cyber incident in which malware later linked by researchers to North Korea's Lazarus Group was found on an isolated administrative network, with plant operations reported unaffected.

Hackers were inside South Korea's diplomat training system for 9 months — Should Read

Hackers compromised the Korea National Diplomatic Academy’s e-learning platform for about nine months, exposing IDs, names, emails and encrypted passwords of current and former South Korean foreign ministry personnel. Officials say the intrusion involved a zero-day flaw and misconfigured security settings, but they have not attributed it to any group.

  • Unidentified hackers compromised the Korea National Diplomatic Academy’s e-learning platform from April 2025 to February 2026.
  • South Korea’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the exposed data is believed to include trainee IDs, names, email addresses, and encrypted passwords, while contact details and personal photos were not affected.
  • The ministry shut down the system after being notified of abnormal access by a related government authority and had not restored it as of the announcement.
  • JoongAng Daily reported that the attacker exploited a previously unknown zero-day vulnerability in the server software, along with misconfigured security settings, to access the network.
  • The ministry said it could not yet determine exactly what information had been accessed or exfiltrated during the compromise.

Software provider to more than 2,000 US hospitals says hackers stole employee and customer data — Should Read

Craneware, a UK software provider used by more than 2,000 U.S. hospitals, said hackers accessed its internal network and stole some employee, customer and partner data. The company says the intrusion is contained, services were not disrupted, and it is still determining whether any sensitive or patient data was taken.

  • Craneware said hackers gained unauthorized access to a subset of its data environment and stole data on employees, customers and business partners.
  • The company said the intrusion has been contained, the attackers no longer have access to its systems, and its operations and hospital services were not disrupted.
  • Craneware reported the incident to the FBI and Britain’s Information Commissioner’s Office and brought in outside forensic investigators.
  • The company said many file names were viewed and copied, mostly involving non-sensitive or publicly available regulatory data, but some employee and customer and partner records were also taken.
  • Craneware has not said who was responsible, when the hackers first gained access, how long they were inside, whether an extortion demand was made, or whether patient information was stolen.

New 7-Zip Vulnerability Could Let Crafted XZ Archives Run Code During Extraction — Should Read

7-Zip fixed a high-severity heap buffer overflow in its XZ archive handling that could allow code execution when a victim opens a crafted archive. Users should manually update to 7-Zip 26.02 or later, especially on systems that handle archives from untrusted sources.

  • CVE-2026-14266 is a heap-based buffer overflow in 7-Zip’s handling of XZ chunked data that could allow code execution when a crafted XZ archive is opened.
  • 7-Zip fixed the flaw in version 26.02, which was released on June 25 before Trend Micro’s Zero Day Initiative detailed the issue on July 15.
  • ZDI rated the flaw 7.0, or High, with a local attack vector and required user interaction, rather than a network-reachable or no-click issue.
  • As of July 20, 2026, The Hacker News found no public proof-of-concept and no credible report of exploitation in the wild.
  • Users should update manually to 7-Zip 26.02 or later, and products that ship a vulnerable copy of 7-Zip’s XZ decoder need their own vendor fixes.

Microsoft confirms Windows Server Update Services sync delays — Should Read

Microsoft confirmed ongoing WSUS synchronization delays and timeouts that can prevent admins from deploying the latest Windows updates via WSUS or Configuration Manager. Mitigations are in place for new or rebuilt WSUS servers, but Microsoft is still working on a safe fix for already affected environments.

  • Microsoft is working to fix a known issue affecting Windows Server Update Services servers that has caused synchronization problems for more than a week.
  • Affected WSUS servers may experience increased synchronization times or sync operation timeouts, preventing administrators from deploying the latest Windows updates through WSUS or Configuration Manager.
  • Microsoft said the issue affects client platforms starting with Windows 10 version 1607 and later, and server platforms starting with Windows Server 2012 and later.
  • Microsoft rolled out mitigation measures on Saturday that restored normal synchronization for new WSUS installations and rebuilt WSUS servers.
  • Microsoft is still working on mitigation steps to help customers safely remove affected metadata from previously affected WSUS environments.

How a Fortune 500 media company blocked a Scattered Lapsus ShinyHunters attack using infrastructure flagged 24 hours before it launched — Should Read

A Fortune 500 media company blocked a Scattered Lapsus ShinyHunters social engineering campaign because Silent Push had flagged and mapped the attacker infrastructure 24 hours before it was used. After the first attempt, the company pushed related domains to CrowdStrike, stopping a second attempt minutes later.

  • A Fortune 500 media and entertainment company stopped a Scattered Lapsus ShinyHunters attack because Silent Push had flagged the attacker infrastructure one day before the attack launched.
  • The threat actor called an employee and directed them to a lookalike domain impersonating a passkey authentication flow.
  • CrowdStrike detected the outbound connection attempt in firewall logs, and the security team used Silent Push to confirm the domain was an Indicator of Future Attack.
  • The organization used Silent Push to enumerate related campaign domains and pushed them into its CrowdStrike firewall within minutes.
  • Fifteen minutes after the initial domain was blocked, a second social engineering attempt against a different employee using a different domain was already blocked.

The PayPal Scam That Emailed You Your Own Password — May Read

A fake PayPal renewal email bypassed major filters by using an authenticated unrelated domain, no links, and no attachments, instead pushing the victim to call a phone number after showing a fabricated credential block with their own email. The key lesson is that clean authentication and link scanning are not enough; callback phishing must be detected by behavioral signals like brand mismatch, urgency, unsolicited credentials, and phone-only calls to action.

  • A manufacturing executive received a fake PayPal Goods Protection renewal email claiming a 599 USD charge and listing the recipient’s own corporate email address as the username.
  • The message contained no link and no attachment, and its only call to action was a callback phone number embedded in the body text.
  • The email was sent from no-reply@verificationemail.com, an unrelated domain authorized to send through Amazon Simple Email Service and aligned with DKIM, allowing it to clear DMARC at the receiving gateway.
  • Barracuda scored the message 0.15 against a quarantine threshold of 3.0, while Microsoft assigned it a Spam Confidence Level of -1.
  • IRONSCALES Adaptive AI flagged the message at 90 percent confidence by analyzing behavior such as the unrelated sender, PayPal impersonation in the body, fabricated credential disclosure, urgency around a charge, and a phone-only call to action.

More than 1,000 domains illegally streaming World Cup games seized, DOJ says — May Read

The DOJ said it seized more than 1,000 domains used to illegally stream World Cup matches, warning that such piracy sites can expose users to malware and payment theft. The operation involved HSI and international partners, with related takedowns and arrests across Latin America and other regions.

  • The Department of Justice announced that more than 1,000 domains used to illegally stream World Cup games were seized during the tournament.
  • The domains were disabled in three successive operations led by Homeland Security Investigations and the National Intellectual Property Rights Coordination Center.
  • Federal officials said the effort was also meant to address risks to consumers from malicious software embedded in many illicit streaming services.
  • The international investigation led to additional site takedowns across Argentina, Ecuador, Peru, Brazil, the Dominican Republic and Colombia.
  • Colombian authorities arrested four suspected members of Los Ciberinfiltrados, a cyber gang accused of illegally accessing telecommunication systems and selling pirated streaming content since 2024.

Windows KB5121767 OOB update fixes shutdowns on some Dell PCs — May Read

Microsoft released emergency out-of-band updates KB5121767 and KB5121768 to fix a Windows 11 issue that caused some Dell PCs with Intel IPF drivers to suffer shutdowns, poor performance, overheating, and battery drain after recent updates. Affected Dell devices that were blocked from the July 2026 security update can now install the fix.

  • Microsoft released emergency updates to fix a known issue causing some Dell PCs to experience performance problems or shut down after installing the July 2026 Windows 11 security updates.
  • The issue affects Dell systems that installed the KB5101650 cumulative update on Windows 11 25H2 and 24H2 devices.
  • Microsoft said the root cause is an incompatibility between the Intel Innovation Platform Framework Processor Participant driver and the new Windows USB-C Connection Manager interface introduced in the June 23, 2026 KB5095093 preview cumulative update.
  • Affected devices may show a yellow exclamation mark in Device Manager next to the Intel Innovation Platform Framework Processor Participant driver and can experience unexpected shutdowns, poor performance, increased heat, and battery drain.
  • Microsoft released KB5121767 for Windows 11 25H2 and 24H2 and KB5121768 for Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC 2024, and said affected Dell devices that were temporarily blocked from the July 2026 security update can now install the out-of-band update.

Flock Safety kills acoustic system designed to detect 'human distress' — May Read

Flock Safety is dropping its acoustic “Distress Detection” system, which aimed to detect gunshots, screaming, and other signs of human distress, after privacy and civil liberties backlash. The company said the feature was only in limited trials and could not understand speech or identify voices.

  • Flock Safety is abandoning plans to sell an acoustic gunshot detection device that could detect screaming and other types of “human distress.”
  • Flock said in a July 10 blog post that the feature was only available to a small number of customers in a limited trial and was never broadly released.
  • Flock said the decision to remove the product followed “community consultation” and emphasized that the system could not understand speech, analyze language, or identify voices.
  • The Electronic Frontier Foundation criticized the system over civil liberties concerns, the possibility of sending armed police to loud street interactions, and potential conflicts with state eavesdropping laws.
  • The Los Angeles Police Department recently announced it would cut ties with Flock Safety while seeking more protections for how Flock-collected information is managed and stored.

2026 Health-ISAC CISO Benchmarking Report — Optional

Health-ISAC’s first CISO Benchmarking Report summarizes survey input from 76 health-sector CISOs on key security risks, budgets, workforce challenges, framework maturity, and AI’s growing role in both defense and threats. The main takeaway is that healthcare security leaders are increasing investment and maturity while still struggling to keep pace with escalating cyber risk, staffing shortages, and emerging technologies.

  • Health-ISAC published its first CISO Benchmarking Report on July 20, 2026.
  • The report reflects survey input from 76 CISOs representing Providers, Payers, Pharma, Medical Devices, and Global Operations.
  • The report says health sector organizations operate in a high-stakes threat environment where cyber breaches can delay care, put patient safety at risk, and undermine trust in the institution.
  • The report covers challenges and threats, the CISO role, budget and spending, the security workforce, framework alignment, and AI and emerging technology.
  • The report states that cybersecurity budgets in the health sector are growing, while workforce shortages continue to shape what security programs can realistically accomplish.

Mythos Didn't Break Your Security Program. Your Exposure Window Could. — Optional

The article argues that AI-driven vulnerability discovery like Anthropic’s Mythos makes the key security metric the exposure window: how long critical systems remain exploitable before remediation. Organizations should focus less on raw CVE volume and more on rapidly mobilizing fixes and reducing attack paths to critical assets.

  • The article argues that the exposure window, defined as the time between when a vulnerability becomes exploitable and when it is fixed, is the key metric for whether vulnerabilities lead to breaches.
  • The author says AI-driven discovery from Anthropic’s Mythos did not create the exposure window but widened it by adding pressure to an already overloaded vulnerability management pipeline.
  • The article states that attackers’ eCrime breakout time averaged 29 minutes in 2025, while PCI DSS allows 30 days to remediate a critical vulnerability.
  • The author identifies mobilization, including ownership, remediation, approvals, and organizational complexity, as the stage where continuous threat exposure management programs commonly break down.
  • The article recommends focusing remediation on attack paths that connect exploitable exposures to critical assets, so organizations can reduce the reachable “blast radius” rather than trying to fix every exposure equally.

Governing Agentic AI at the Decision Point: AWS + Netskope — Optional

The article argues that production agentic AI needs both deterministic tool-call authorization and semantic content inspection: AWS AgentCore Policy controls whether an agent may call a tool with specific parameters, while Netskope One AI Guardrails checks prompts and tool responses for injection, unsafe content, and data leakage.

  • Agentic AI deployments often harden prompts but spend little time securing what happens after the model decides to call a tool.
